title: Great God, This Sacred Day of Thine
description: Great God, This Sacred Day of Thine in Tonic Solfa to MELITA, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Anne Steele wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 10 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “A Prayer for Lord's Day”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELITA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: Great God, this sa-cred day of thine De-mands our souls' col-lect-ed powers. May we em-ploy in work di-vine These sol-emn, these de-vot-ed hours; O may our souls a-dor-ing own The grace which calls us to thy throne.

lines: Great God, this sacred day of thine
Demands our souls' collected powers.
May we employ in work divine
These solemn, these devoted hours;
O may our souls adoring own
The grace which calls us to thy throne.
Hence, ye vain cares and trifles, fly;
Where God resides appear no more;
Omniscient God, thy piercing eye
Can every secret thought explore:
O may thy grace our hearts refine,
And fix our thoughts on things divine.
The word of life dispensed to-day
Invites us to a heavenly feast.
May every ear the call obey;
Be every heart a humble guest;
O bid the wretched sons of need
On soul-reviving dainties feed.
Thy spirit's powerful aid impart;
O may thy word, with life divine,
Engage the ear, and warm the heart;
Then shall the day indeed be thine;
Then shall our souls adoring own
The grace which calls us to thy throne.

licence: Public domain: Anne Steele died in 1778.
credits: Words by Anne Steele (1717–1778), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELITA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
